claim: Carrières des Lumières 2026 hours are seasonal: Jan/Nov/Dec 10am–6pm; Feb/Mar 9:30am–6pm; Apr–Jun & Sep/Oct 9:30am–7pm; Jul/Aug 9am–7:30pm; last admission one hour before closing.
quote: January, November, December: 10am–6pm. February & March: 9:30am–6pm. April, May, June, September, October: 9:30am–7pm. July & August: 9am–7:30pm. Last admission occurs one hour before closing.

claim: Carrières des Lumières individual adult ticket in 2026 is €16.50, seniors €15.50, students/7–25 €14, family €46; combined Pass Baux-de-Provence (Carrières + Château) is €21 adult, €19.50 senior, €17.50 student, €16 child 7–17, €58 family.
quote: Adults: €16.50; Seniors (65+): €15.50; Students & ages 7–25: €14; Family: €46. Pass Baux-de-Provence: Adults: €21; Seniors: €19.50; Students/18–25: €17.50; Children 7–17: €16; Family: €58.

claim: The 2026 Carrières des Lumières program is Picasso 'L'art en mouvement' (40-min long programme, 450+ images covering painting, drawing, engraving, sculpture, ceramics, collage) plus a short Frida Kahlo programme 'En plein cœur' (14 min), opening 13 February 2026.
quote: Du 13 février 2026… plus de 450 images d'œuvres, de photographies et d'archives… 'Picasso, l'art en mouvement'… accompagnée d'un programme court dédié à Frida Kahlo… 'Frida Kahlo, en plein cœur'… 14 minutes.

claim: Château des Baux is open every day all year (closed 25 December); 2026 seasonal hours: Jan/Feb/Nov/Dec 10am–5pm; Mar/Oct 9:30am–6pm; Apr/May/Jun/Sep 9am–7pm; Jul/Aug 9am–7:30pm.
quote: Ouvert tous les jours toute l'année — Open everyday all year round. January, February, November and December: 10.00 am to 5.00 pm; March, October: 9.30 am to 6.00 pm; April, May, June, September: 9.00 am to 7.00 pm; July, August: 9.00 am to 7.30 pm.

claim: Château des Baux 2026 admission: adult €10, senior €9, child 7–17 €7, family (2+2) €27, under-7 free; the site spans 7 hectares with reconstructed medieval siege engines (trebuchet, ballista) on the plateau.
quote: Adults: 10€; Seniors (over 65): 9€; Children (under 7): free; Children 7 to 17 years: 7€; Family (2 adults + 2 children aged 7 to 17): 27€.

claim: The Château hosts the largest collection of full-scale reconstructed medieval siege machines in Europe (trebuchet, ballista, battering ram, couillard), with live firing demonstrations using real projectiles in season from costumed staff.
quote: Catapult demonstrations typically occur at 11:00 am, 3:30 pm, and 5:30 pm daily… reconstructions of medieval siege engines such as catapults and trebuchets… shooting demonstrations every day using real projectiles.

claim: The Carrières quarry was repurposed as 'Cathédrale d'Images' by Albert Plécy in 1975 with the first audiovisual show on Easter Monday 1977; after his death and Anne Plécy's death in 2002, the city handed management to Culturespaces in 2008 and the site reopened in 2012 as Carrières de Lumières.
quote: Albert Plécy established the 'Cathedral of Images' in the white limestone quarries of Les Baux-de-Provence in 1975… The first performance took place on Easter Monday 1977… In 2008, the city… entrust management to Culturespaces, and the site reopened in 2012 under the name Carrières de Lumières.

claim: The Pavillon de la Reine Jeanne is a hexagonal Renaissance corner-pavilion built ~1568–1581 for Jeanne de Quiqueran in the Vallon de la Fontaine below the village; Frédéric Mistral had a replica built for his tomb in Maillane.
quote: Renaissance style built for Jeanne de Quiqueran… nestled in the Vallon de la Fontaine near the old washhouse… hexagonal plan… Frédéric Mistral had a replica built for his tomb in Maillane.

claim: The 12th–16th century Église Saint-Vincent is partly carved into the rock and contains the de Manville flamboyant Gothic funerary chapel and modern stained-glass windows by Max Ingrand, donated by Prince Rainier III of Monaco.
quote: Built between the 12th and 16th centuries, the Church of Saint-Vincent is partly carved out of the rock… funerary chapel of the de Manville family, with its flamboyant Gothic vault, and Max Ingrand's modern stained-glass windows, donated… by Prince Rainier III of Monaco.

claim: L'Oustau de Baumanière is roughly 0.1 mi (≈200 m) from Carrières des Lumières — under a 5-minute walk — and the quarry sits under 10 minutes' walk from the village core.
quote: L'Oustau de Baumaniere is 0.1 mi from Carrières des Lumières… Carrières are less than 10 minutes walk from the village of Les Baux-de-Provence.

claim: Les Baux's main street is dense with lavender-soaped souvenir shops and overpriced snacks; the consensus workaround is to arrive early morning or stay into late afternoon after the day-trippers leave, or visit off-season (Sep–Oct).
quote: Les Baux is incredibly touristy and filled with shop after shop… overpriced, from souvenirs to snacks to meals… Stay late in the day, after the tour buses leave; spend the night… or come off-season.

claim: Practical visitor advice: village is fully pedestrian with multiple paid lots at the base that fill even in winter; arrive in the morning for parking and cooler air, return for late-afternoon light when buses depart; allow a half-day for château + village + Carrières.
quote: Multiple paid lots accommodate cars and campers around the village base… in high summer it is best to arrive early in the day… linger into late afternoon to enjoy better light once day-trippers depart.
